# Actual shell signatures and a finite critical-response test

This note connects the proved shared-source cap credit to an ACTUAL body first variation. It gives a sufficient finite-menu test, and an exact critical example where crossing is positive but that test does not pay. It asserts no global assembly theorem.

## 1. Actual compatible contraction and shell laws

Let positive full-dimensional fibers K_z belong to one actual mixed convex body. Select distinct fibers indexed by I={s} union A union B, with the two anchored relations (1) from `candidate c7b6ab042f325988`. Choose c_z in int K_z for z in I. Suppose the simultaneous replacements

    K_z(epsilon)=c_z+(1-epsilon)(K_z-c_z), z in I,
    K_z(epsilon)=K_z, z not in I,                         (1)

are the exact fibers of actual convex bodies for every sufficiently small epsilon>=0. This compatibility is a hypothesis, not inferred from independent fiber contraction. It will be checked explicitly in Section 4.

Write V_z=|K_z| and A=sum_(z in I) V_z. The removed shell has volume

    Delta_z(epsilon)=tau(epsilon)V_z,
    tau(epsilon)=1-(1-epsilon)^d,
    M'(0+)=-d A.                                        (2)

For each source let nu_z be its normalized cone probability measure on boundary K_z about c_z. It can be defined without smoothness: for a Borel boundary set E, its cone has volume V_z nu_z(E). For polytopes, on a facet F at distance h_F>0 from c_z it has density h_F/(dV_z) relative to facet area. The cones partition K_z up to a null set. Consequently, if U_z has law nu_z and R_epsilon is independent with density

    d r^(d-1)/tau(epsilon), 1-epsilon<r<1,

then c_z+R_epsilon(U_z-c_z) is uniform on the removed shell. This follows by radial integration on each cone; for general convex bodies it follows directly from the scaling law for the defining cones.

Take any two couplings of the nu_z laws in the two relations, sharing the same nu_s marginal, and glue them conditionally on U_s. The construction in the preceding shared-source note applies to their full three-bit signatures as well. Add one common independent R_epsilon and form all the shell variables as above. Each source marginal is its ACTUAL uniform shell law. The two barycentric outputs lie in the original target K_p by convex compatibility, even though they need not lie in its deformed version. Only the original target is used for this implication.

For a fixed closed ambient cap H_j, suppose its boundary has zero probability under both limiting barycentric output laws and all the source cone laws. Let f_(r,j),o_j denote the limiting two target probabilities and their intersection, under ONE common gluing. All affine margins of shell variables converge pointwise to the corresponding boundary-variable margins. Dominated convergence then preserves the entire finite joint signature table, not merely separate marginal probabilities.

Apply the POINTWISE hitting-cost proof of the shared-source theorem to the finite shell variables. The shells themselves are not convex, and no convex-source hypothesis is invoked: that proof needs only the actual uniform marginals and the affine indicator implications, both already established here. Its coefficients are all multiplied by tau(epsilon), because the shell volumes have that common factor. Divide by epsilon and pass to the limit. With

    a=d V_s, b=d min_A V_z, c=d min_B V_z,
    c1=min(a,b), c2=min(a,c), c12=min(a,b+c),
    rho=c1+c2-c12,

and

    L_j=lim_(epsilon down 0)
             sum_(z in I)| (K_z\K_z(epsilon)) intersect H_j |/epsilon,

one obtains the actual loss inequality

    L_j >= B_j:=c1 f_(1,j)+c2 f_(2,j)-rho o_j.       (3)

The existence of L_j follows from the same radial representation. The strictness over fixed independent packing is again exactly rho[min(f_1,f_2)-o_j]. No source loss is counted twice.

The boundary-null hypotheses above are explicit. They hold in the example below. Supporting coincidences instead require the allocated traces in the nonsmooth finite-menu theorem; the present note does not silently identify their cone traces with closed cap indicators.

## 2. Connection to a proper critical circuit

Fix a genuine critical circuit of closed caps H_j through an actual deepest source, with raw cap mass Q=beta M. Let the continuous normals u_j be normalized to unit length, rho_j>0 satisfy sum rho_j u_j=0, and let the original weighted margin cover the circuit's assigned deepest base planes. Assume every fiber trace is proper or strictly full/empty, with no positive-area supporting coincidences. Put

    S_j=sum_z H_(d-1)(K_z intersect boundary H_j)>0.

These are the regular coarea hypotheses in `candidate 07dbcd642c33993d`. Its displayed response calculation uses no simplex property and applies directly to the polytopal fibers here. Under the actual contraction (1) and threshold shifts s_j, the cap derivative is

    D_j=-L_j-S_j s_j.

Equalizing these derivatives subject to sum rho_j s_j=0 gives exactly

    q_c=-sum_j theta_j L_j,
    theta_j=(rho_j/S_j)/(sum_h rho_h/S_h).          (4)

This follows by solving s_j=(-L_j-q_c)/S_j and summing. In particular the same actual body deformation gives strict normalized response descent at this witness if

    sum_j theta_j B_j > beta d A.                 (5)

Indeed (3) and (4) imply q_c < -beta d A=beta M'. The finite quantile response supplies cover-preserving thresholds, with strict cap-mass decrease relative to the changing total volume.

Equation (5) is a SUFFICIENT test; failure says nothing about the exact L_j. For a finite menu, select one circuit at each assigned deepest witness. Condition (5) must hold separately for EVERY selected circuit with the SAME actual body variation (1). Finitely many uniformly slack covers at the unassigned bases must also persist, as in the finite-menu theorem. Only under those assumptions does the resulting variation strictly decrease global normalized maximum depth. A weighted average of (5) over witnesses is not enough.

Within one three-cap circuit, optimize the ONE conditional 8 by 8 signature transport using weights theta_j. The finite Borel selection and kernel-lifting proof in the shared-source note retains both original relation couplings and all three caps. It may optimize sum theta_j B_j; it does not choose incompatible per-cap intersections. The theta_j are fixed by actual proper section measures, not freely assigned.

## 3. A useful logical distinction

The original shared-source volume inequality applies to any actual couplings of uniform FIBER laws. The response test (5) uses uniform SHELL laws and their cone-measure limits. These laws differ. A gain established only for volume-uniform target copies cannot be inserted into (5) without this separate shell construction.

Likewise the barycentric outputs need not be new candidate centers. Their role is to certify losses of genuine critical caps at the already specified witnesses. The selected point and all normals remain those of the actual finite response theorem.

## 4. Complete actual five-fiber critical calibration

Take n=1,d=2, integer bases -2,-1,0,1,2, and centered rectangles with halfwidth pairs

    (1,1), (5/2,7/4), (3,2), (5/2,7/4), (1,1).   (6)

Interpolate both halfwidth functions affinely between consecutive bases. Both are positive and have strictly decreasing successive slopes, so this describes one compact convex body with interior and exactly those integer fibers. Its mixed set is centrally symmetric about (0,0,0). The fiber areas are

    4, 35/2, 24, 35/2, 4; total M=67.

Every nonvertical through-origin ambient cap has exactly M/2 captured mass: central reflection interchanges its strict sides, and its boundary has zero area in every fiber. For any candidate point, choose a continuous linear functional which is positive on its continuous coordinate, or any such functional if that coordinate is zero. Its containing threshold cap has mass at most M/2 by the same reflection pairing. Thus the actual maximum raw depth is Q=M/2=67/2, attained at the origin. In particular every cylindrical through-origin cap used below is genuinely globally critical there.

Use target p=0, shared source s=-1, exclusive sets A={1},B={2}, and relations

    0=(-1+1)/2=(2/3)(-1)+(1/3)2.                  (7)

Contract exactly fibers -1,1,2 about their centers by factor 1-epsilon, leaving the other fibers fixed. For x halfwidths, the three discrete second differences become

    -1+5epsilon, -1-5epsilon, -1+4epsilon.

For y halfwidths they become

    -1/2+(7/2)epsilon, -1/2-(7/2)epsilon,
                                      -1/2+(5/2)epsilon.

All remain negative for 0<=epsilon<1/7, so the simultaneous shell variation is ACTUALLY convex-compatible. Its total derivative is m=-2(35/2+35/2+4)=-78.

For a centered rectangle, normalized cone measure selects each of the four faces with probability1/4 and is uniform along that face. Hence use a common Z with that law on boundary[-1,1]^2 and source boundary variables

    U_-1=U_1=((5/2)Z_x,(7/4)Z_y), U_2=(Z_x,Z_y).

The limiting target variables are

    Y_1=((5/2)Z_x,(7/4)Z_y),
    Y_2=(2 Z_x,(3/2)Z_y).                         (8)

Use the actual critical circuit

    H_1={x+y>=0}, H_2={-x+y>=0}, H_3={-y>=0}.      (9)

All source and output boundary probabilities on these lines are zero. For the first two caps, both target probabilities are1/2, and each directed crossing probability is1/160. For example, on the top square face their respective x-coordinate thresholds are -7/10 and -3/4; the interval between them has length1/20, hence cone probability (1/4)(1/40)=1/160. The bottom face gives the reverse crossing. The other faces contribute none. For H_3 the target events coincide.

Here a=b=35,c=8, so c1=c12=35,c2=rho=8. The best fixed independent loss bound is35/2 in every cap. The adaptive bounds are

    B_1=B_2=35/2+1/20=351/20,
    B_3=35/2.                                    (10)

For the raw normals in (9) the dependence coefficients are (1,1,2). Raw-threshold coareas are (15,15,20), so normalization to unit normals in (4) gives the invariant weights

    theta=(2/7,2/7,3/7).

Thus one common shell gluing gives the strict weighted gain

    sum theta_j B_j=35/2+1/35=1227/70             (11)

over fixed packing. Nevertheless the response threshold in (5) is beta d A=39. The exact actual cap losses are L_j=39 for all three j, because each selected source rectangle and its shell are centrally symmetric and each cap passes through its center. Therefore

    q_c=-39=beta m,

and this genuine critical circuit gives NO strict normalized first-order descent.

This remains true for any finite menu consisting entirely of cylindrical through-origin circuits under this contraction: each cap loss is39, and every circuit response equals beta m. Selecting among such circuits does not change the answer. Other critical tilted caps exist; no conclusion is asserted for a menu enlarged to include them.

The example proves a precise limitation while retaining the new information: adaptive crossing can strictly improve an actual loss certificate, for the SAME real deformation and a genuine critical circuit, without paying its normalized response. The decisive next requirement is an inequality of the form (5) at each selected witness, not merely positivity of crossing or its average over caps.

## 5. A genuine selected-menu switch and the information it uses

The preceding body also supplies an exact favorable critical circuit. Replace (9) by

    H'_1={x+y+10z>=0}, H'_2={-x+y+10z>=0},
    H'_3={-y+10z>=0}.                              (12)

At every positive base all three caps are strictly full, and at every negative base strictly empty. At base0 they are the same proper through-center caps as before. Their initial masses are all

    24/2+35/2+4=67/2=Q.

Thus they are genuinely critical. Their continuous positive circuit still covers the entire base0 plane. Strict full/empty traces have no supporting coincidences and contribute no proper coarea, so the regular response formula still applies. Strict full/empty fibers contribute only their ordinary body-loss term, so formula (4) applies without a supporting allocation.

For the actual contraction of Section4, each cap loses the FULL selected positive fibers1 and2, and none of fiber-1. Hence L'_j=2(35/2+4)=43 in every row, and q'=-43<beta m=-39. In fact, writing tau=1-(1-epsilon)^2, the exact masses are

    M_epsilon=67-39tau,
    |S_epsilon intersect H'_j|=67/2-(43/2)tau
                             =M_epsilon/2-2tau.    (13)

All full/empty classifications persist for epsilon<1/7. Every point on the middle base belongs to at least one cap in (12), so its raw depth is at most the second quantity in (13).

The other bases have explicit uniformly slack covers. At base1, two opposite continuous normals with a sufficiently large positive integer tilt include fiber2, exclude every lower base, and cut fiber1 through its center. Their union covers the base1 plane and each mass is at most4+35/4=51/4. At base-1 use the negative integer tilt, with the same bound. At the endpoints the analogous isolating pair gives bound2. These covers persist under the nested centered contraction, with masses no larger. For epsilon<1/7, (13) remains above51/4. Thus (12) proves a STRICT decrease of the actual global normalized maximum depth. No assertion about its exact new value is required.

At the shared target p=0, the added base tilt vanishes. Therefore BOTH limiting target variables have exactly the SAME joint three-bit signature law as in Section4. The raw coareas of (12) are (4,4,6), giving weights (3/10,3/10,2/5); the adaptive weighted lower bound is only

    (3/10)(351/20)+(3/10)(351/20)+(2/5)(35/2)
       =1753/100 <39.

It does not certify the real payment43. The changed source traces are decisive: the exclusive positive-base fibers are captured even in many samples where their barycentric targets are missed. That actual surplus is retained by the exact source-budget identity in the multi-input coupling theorem, but is discarded by the minimal hitting-set cost in (3).

This is a finite selected-menu test with complete geometry: the zero-tilt menu has no strict response, the tilted menu has a strict actual response, and the output signature law itself does not detect that change. It does not disprove the shared-source inequality; it identifies the additional actual source surplus that a global use must keep.
